text: Dongfang Electric (1072.HK)
Decent New Order Growth; More Gas Turbine Sales to Data Centers
CITI'S TAKE

We hosted an investor call with Dongfang Electric ('DF') on 9 Jul. The company has had steady operational performance year to date. Its new orders were +10% yoy in 5M26, in line with its full-year target. Order backlog was +7% to Rmb150bn by end 5M26. Our 2026-28E net profits are cut 1-6% on more prudent revenue and margin assumptions. Our DF TP is -44% to HK\$30/share based on 15x 2027E PER. We attribute its share price pullback in recent months as likely owing to more realistic revenue realization from its gas turbine export (Rmb2bn pa or <3% total revenue in 2026-27E and Rmb6bn or 7% of total revenue in 2028E). DF is our top pick in the PRC power plant equipment sector with the most diversified product mix. Its 11.2x 2027E PER is not high. We transfer coverage of DF to Pierre Lau from Bella Tian.

Rising gas turbine production capacity amid high demand — DF has gas turbine production capacity of 50MW each of 10-12 units pa. The production capacity would rise to 30 units by end 2027E after Ph.1 expansion at capex of Rmb760m. Ph.2 expansion is in planning. The company has orders on hand of 20 sets for gas turbine generators of 50MW each so that its gas turbine production capacity would be running at full utilization in 2025-26E with 12-month lead time.

Getting new orders for gas turbine exports for data centers — DF signed new orders for sales of 10 units at Rmb150-200m each in 1H26 expecting to make GP margin >30%. The products are for data centers in Canada with the orders placed by their representatives in mainland China; orders for another 10 units could be signed from the same customer in 2H26E. Inquiries from the US data centers could render more new orders ahead, pending UL certification from the US (while Canadian certification has already been secured). DF also provides after-sale services as well as repairs & maintenance for these exports. DF sold its 50MW gas turbine to Kazakhstan previously.

Decent product quality — The energy conversion efficiency of DF's 50MW gas turbine is 64%, 2ppts below those made by Siemens. DF views its gas turbine sales as competitive in terms of pricing and delivery time. 80-90% of gas turbine sales proceeds are received on product delivery. Meanwhile, DF's capacity expansion to make 200MW gas turbines under cooperation with Mitsubishi Heavy (7011 JT, Buy) is in planning stage. Such potential product could be made in 2028E and used in the domestic market.

text: Dongfang Electric (1072.HK)
10 July 2026
Citi
Satisfactory Business Performance

We hosted an investor call with Dongfang Electric ('DF') on 9 Jul. The company has had steady operational performance year to date. Its new orders were up 10% yoy in 5M26, in line with its full-year target to rise the same extent. Its new orders were Rmb117.2bn in 2025, including Rmb5.4bn or 4.6% from overseas. Order backlog was +7% to Rmb150bn by end 5M26, from Rmb140bn by end 2025. Revenue and profit growth were on-track year to date.
More Gas Turbine Sales to Overseas Data Centers

DF has gas turbine production capacity of 50MW each of 10-12 units pa. The production capacity would rise to 30 units by end 2027E after Ph.1 expansion at capex of Rmb760m. Ph.2 expansion is in planning. The company has orders on hand of 20 sets for gas turbine generators of 50MW each so that its gas turbine production capacity will be running at full utilization in 2025-26E with 12-month lead time.

New orders were signed in 1H26 for sales of 10 units at Rmb150-200m each making GP margin >30% to data centers in Canada placed by their representatives in mainland China; orders for another 10 units could be signed from the same customer in 2H26E. Inquiries from the US data centers could render more new orders ahead, pending UL certification from the US (while Canadian certification has already been secured). DF also provides after-sale services as well as repairs & maintenance for these exports. It sold its 50MW gas turbine to Kazakhstan previously.

The energy conversion efficiency of DF's 50MW gas turbine is $64\%$ , 2ppts below those made by Siemens. DF views its gas turbine sales as competitive in terms of pricing and delivery time. $80 - 90\%$ of gas turbine sales proceeds are received on product delivery.

DF's capacity expansion to make 200MW gas turbines under cooperation with Mitsubishi Heavy (7011 JT, Buy) is in planning. Such potential product probably could be made in 2028E and used in the domestic market.
Revenue Rise of Hydropower Equipment from Pump Storage

DF forecasts its revenue from hydropower equipment sales to rise to Rmb10bn in 2029/30E (comprising 80% from pump storage facilities), from Rmb3.9bn in 2025. Its orders for hydropower equipment kept rising mainly driven by more demand for pumped-storage facilities. To recap, PRC government targets to add 100GW newly commissioned pumped storage capacity in the 15 $^{th}$ five-year period (2026-30E) so that PRC pumped storage facilities would rise to around 160GW by end 2030E, which would be 2.6x of 62GW by end 2025. This massive buildout is designed to coordinate with the 300GW ESS so that China would have total 460GW energy storage resources to stabilize power grids and facilitate the increase of PRC non-fossil power generation mix to 50% by 2030E.

DF guides the GP margin of its hydropower equipment sales could rise to 15-18%, from 12% in 2025, boosted by more pump storage equipment sales. New orders from the world's largest hydropower project to be built on the lower reaches of Yanlung Zangbo River in Tibet would start to receive from 2028E.

Dongfang Electric (1072.HK)
10 July 2026
Citi
Other Business Updates

1. Less market tendering of coal-fired power equipment in China – PRC market bidding of coal-fired power equipment demand could drop from 80GW pa in previous years to 50GW pa in 2026-30E estimated by DF, though the company's revenue from coal-fired power equipment sales would rise yoy in 2026E based on orders on hand. The sales prices of 2x1,000MW thermal power equipment is Rmb1.1bn; and DF assumes GP margin of this business to be steady around 20-22% (vs. 20.7% in 2025).

2. Revenue rise from nuclear equipment sales – DF guides PRC newly approved nuclear construction to remain at 10 units pa in the 15 $^{th}$ FYP. Its revenue from nuclear equipment sales could rise from Rmb5.7bn in 2025 to Rmb8bn pa in coming years depending on delivery schedule.
3. Low margin of wind turbine sales - DF estimates its revenue from wind equipment sales to rise 10% yoy to Rmb20bn in 2026E; GP margin of this business (3% in 2025) would remain low.

Dongfang Electric
Company description

Dongfang is one of China's top three manufacturers of power-generation equipment. It has the capability of making engines, turbines and boilers for coal-fired, gas, hydro, nuclear and wind power plants.
Investment strategy

We maintain Dongfang Electric ("DF") Buy rating, benefiting from (i) large exposure to potential overseas gas turbine sales, (ii) robust domestic demand for nuclear and hydropower equipment, and (iii) a smaller profit proportion from coal-fired power equipment sales compared to its peers.
Valuation
Our target price for Dongfang H-shares of HK\$30 is based on 15x 2027E PER which we think reasonable in view of its 17% 2026-28E EPS CAGR.
Risks

Key downside risks that could prevent Dongfang shares from reaching our target price include (i) an increase in steel prices, which would decrease the company's profit margin as its orders on hand are at fixed prices, (ii) a decrease in ASP, which would decrease its revenue and margin, and (iii) weak new order flows.
Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
Valuation

We use a sum-of-the-parts approach to value MHI, using the average for three metrics: PER, EV/sales, and EV/EBIT. Using our FY3/28 sales and OP forecasts for the four main divisions to reflect the longer-term characteristics of the energy and defense businesses in particular, and drawing on a range of international and domestic competitors, factoring in total net debt at end-March 2026 and other balance sheet items, and then applying a 20% subjective premium to reflect the bright long-term outlook for its gas turbine, nuclear, and defense businesses, we arrive at a target price of ¥4,700.
Risks

Factors that could cause the share price to undershoot our target price include: 1) a renewed downturn in civil aerospace with additional losses on the PW1100G engine; 2) greater competition in gas turbines and/or the emergence of a credible Chinese competitor; 3) a nuclear accident; 4) an inability to expand its after-sales activities especially in the energy division; 5) yen strength against the USD; 6) a decision to try again to develop a regional jet (at the behest of the Japanese government); and 7) further losses on the two IGCC projects in Fukushima.

text: Guide to Citi Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:

Citi stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks. Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk rating assigned.

Investment Ratings: Citi investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months. The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval of Citi management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi may suspend its rating and target price and assign "Rating Suspended" status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi may also suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—” and “-” respectively in the rating history price chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi assigned "Under Review" status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the expected total returns may fall outside of these ranges because of market price movements and/or other short-term volatility or trading patterns. Such interim deviations will be permitted but will become subject to review by Research Management. Your decision to buy or sell a security should be based upon your personal investment objectives and should be made only after evaluating the stock's expected performance and risk.
Catalyst Watch/Short Term Views ("STV") Ratings Disclosure:

Catalyst Watch and STV Upside/Downside calls: Citi may also include a Catalyst Watch or STV Upside or Downside call to indicate the analyst expects the share price to rise (fall) in absolute terms over a specified period of 30 or 90 days in reaction to one or more specific near-term catalysts or events impacting the company or the market. A Catalyst Watch will be published when Analyst confidence is high that an impact to share price will occur; it will be a STV when confidence level is moderate. A Catalyst Watch or STV Upside/Downside call will automatically expire at the end of the specified 30/90 day period.
